aria: Animated recap of the Bulls' 117 to 106 road win over the Timberwolves: Buddy Hield's step-back jumper with 5 minutes 43 seconds left in the third quarter that made it 67 to 64 and ended a 13 to 0 Minnesota run, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Norman Powell's 24 points, the top scorers, how the Bulls won, and the next game at Cleveland.

notes: Box score from the Bulls' 117–106 road win over the Minnesota Timberwolves at Target Center on Nov 14, 2026, from the CBS Sports box score and play-by-play, with game details from the Associated Press (via ABC News and CBS Sports), Field Level Media (via The Ticket), Bleacher Nation and Yardbarker. All 117 Chicago points and all 106 Minnesota points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores add up to both totals: 29–17 after one, 58–45 Chicago at the half, 88–80 after three. Team totals (field goals 44 of 90 to 38 of 91, threes 14 of 30 to 9 of 38, free throws 15 of 18 to 21 of 28, assists 29–23) and bench points (50–33) are from the box score. The AP story lists Norman Powell with 23 points; the box score (10 of 19, 3 threes, 1 of 2 at the line) and Field Level Media have 24, which is used here (Bleacher Nation's 51 bench points match the AP count). Rebounds are left out because the sources disagree. Chicago's 16-point lead came at 111–95 with 4:33 left (CBS play-by-play; Yardbarker says as many as 16). Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Saturday's games.

Minnesota missed its first 13 threes and finished 9 of 38 (AP). Minnesota's 13–0 third-quarter run cut a 65–51 deficit to 65–64 (CBS play-by-play; Bleacher Nation); Ayo Dosunmu scored 14 of his 24 in the third (AP). Minnesota got within 113–106 with 1:28 left before Patrick Williams' three made it 116–106 with 1:10 left (CBS play-by-play). The win ended Minnesota's five-game winning streak and gave Chicago consecutive wins for the first time this season (Field Level Media), after Friday's overtime win over Atlanta, in which Powell scored 33. Chicago played without Caleb Wilson, Jalen Smith and Nic Claxton (Bleacher Nation), and arrived on game day after a flight delay (AP). Chicago plays at Cleveland on Monday, Nov 16 at 7:00 PM ET (Yardbarker; AP).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Buddy Hield's jumper with 5:43 left in the third quarter that made it 67–64 and ended Minnesota's 13–0 run (the CBS play-by-play lists it as a two-point step-back jump shot at 5:43, 65–64 to 67–64; Bleacher Nation says Hield 'stopped the bleeding with a pull-up iso jumper'). The shot's distance isn't reported, so it is drawn as the template's pull-up from mid-range. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Chicago Bulls or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Hield’s listed 6-foot-4 and 220 pounds (RealGM), in Chicago's road red with No. 7 (RealGM). No wingspan from a reliable measurement is used, so his arms are drawn at a 1.0 ratio. He has no approved look on file yet, so he is drawn as a team-colour silhouette in the kit. It is an original silhouette with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
